findingDetails.title: Manifest paths can redirect sync writes outside package roots
findingDetails.case: A reviewed vendor.json entry sets local_path to a path such as ../../outside-dir, then an operator runs vendor-sync.py pull.
findingDetails.evidence: resolve_dirs joins local_path and upstream_path without resolving or checking containment. copy_tree removes and replaces the target when include is absent, and its include branch can copy or unlink any joined path. pull_package permits an empty baseline, so that first pull reaches the writes without a drift refusal.
findingDetails.userImpact: A pull or push using changed manifest metadata can overwrite or delete files outside the vendored package and, with traversal, outside the repository or shared-skill tree.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Static audit of resolve_dirs, both copy_tree branches, and pull_package found no absolute-path, parent-component, or resolved-root containment check. Existing scratch tests exercise normal pull/push and include behavior but no escaping path.
findingDetails.recommendation: Before any read or write, reject absolute paths and parent traversal, resolve local_path and upstream_path beneath their designated roots, and resolve every include entry beneath both package roots. Add scratch-world tests proving pull and push refuse escapes without touching the outside target.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The pull preflight refuses a local edit that upstream does not carry, and push refuses upstream drift. Those checks compare file hashes but do not constrain the paths; an empty recorded baseline skips the pull conflict check.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: vendor.json is repository metadata and pull is an explicit operator action, so the paths may be treated as trusted. A changed manifest in a reviewed branch can still redirect the operator's explicit command before the metadata is trusted.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade only if a trusted preflight validates every package and include path beneath its designated root before each mutating command and the CLI refuses otherwise.

findingDetails.title: Plugin build does not reject symlinked hub source files
findingDetails.case: A root hub file such as SKILL.md is a symlink to a file outside the repository when build-plugin.py runs.
findingDetails.evidence: shipped_sources inserts HUB_FILES directly into the source map, while the symlink scan runs only inside the packet os.walk loops. shutil.copyfile follows the hub symlink, and the subsequent source/copy hash comparison succeeds on the copied target bytes.
findingDetails.userImpact: The plugin can ship content not stored at the expected tracked source path, including an unintended local file, while reporting a successful reproducible build.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The hub-file map at lines 71-72 precedes the packet-only symlink check at lines 74-78. The existing self-test plants a symlink under sk-product-owner/references, so it does not cover a HUB_FILES entry.
findingDetails.recommendation: Reject symlinks for every HUB_FILES source before adding it to the map, and add a scratch self-test that plants a symlink at one root hub file and expects refusal.
